newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Tamil and Moslem parties in parliamentary select committee debating government's devolution proposals to meet President Chandrika Kumartunga to try to bring about rapport between government and opposition United National Party.
Justice Minister G.L. Peiris says leaving LTTE out of talks on devolution package to solve ethnic problem will put more pressure on rebels.
Government has given top priority to development of southern province, President Kumaratunga says.
President Kumaratunga urged not to allow withdrawal of army camp at Tantirimale providing security to villages bordering Wilpattu wildlife park.
Millionaire businessman arrested with stock of forged 1,000 rupee notes.
Government planning to dissolve 237 local government bodies in preparation for fresh polls.
Army chief Lt. General Rohan Daluwatte tours Elephant Pass and Paranthan army camps which were attacked last week by Tamil Tiger rebels.
